answer.rationale:
The binding constraint is that the line runs at 94% of committed volume with no buffer and the primary contract lapses in 14 days. Any action that interrupts primary flow raises delivery risk, which the objective forbids, so a clean switch_primary_vendor is not executable inside 14 days at this utilization no matter how attractive the cost story is. That is why I spend the single verification on memory_c2 rather than on the action I intend: c2 is the only inherited record that supports the magnitude of cut finance is demanding, and it is also the record whose transfer conditions are least visible. The consolidated summary says 'moving primary supply to the low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply' but omits the volume, the component's criticality, whether spare buffer existed during onboarding, and whether 'quick onboarding' meant weeks or a quarter. If the original record shows that switch happened on a non-constrained part with inventory cover, the memory does not license a switch here and it also weakens the credibility of any bid I wave at the incumbent. If it shows a comparable constrained part, then a staged qualification becomes the right next-cycle move and I have a real benchmark now.

Intended action is negotiate_terms, held to a short, reversible commitment rather than a multi-year lock. memory_c4 says benchmarking moved the incumbent on both price and payment terms, but I note that record is silent on why they moved -- most likely a credible alternative existed at the time, and my leverage today is exactly as strong as memory_c2 turns out to be. The incumbent has refused to reopen price this cycle, so the recoverable value is in the non-price levers: payment terms, freight, volume tiering, expedite fees. That will not reach 18% alone, and I am not going to pretend it will.

Downstream value risk: memory_c6 makes multi-year commitment look purely good (volume pricing, no scope narrowing), and under an 18% mandate it is tempting to sign a long term to book the discount. That would mortgage next cycle's optionality precisely when add_second_source (memory_c3, the strongest risk-removal evidence here) is the move I want available. memory_c1 similarly reads as clean continuity but was recorded under conditions with no spend mandate. I am deliberately keeping term short so the second-source path stays open, and I am flagging that the residual gap to 18% remains unclosed rather than resolving it with a commitment I cannot reverse. Every one of these memories is a consolidated summary with the source archived; I am treating them as directional, not as measurements.
